name: Plex Media Server
summary: Stream your movies, series and music to TVs, phones and browsers. Media folders on the data volume.

settings.label: Claim token (optional)
settings.help: From https://www.plex.tv/claim, valid for 4 minutes, used only the first time the server starts. Leave empty to claim the server later in the browser.

settings.label: Network mode
settings.help: Host network gives Plex the NAS's own network address: LAN discovery (GDM, DLNA) works and no port needs mapping, but the container is not isolated from the NAS's network. Bridge keeps Plex isolated and publishes only its ports; discovery may not work and the address below may be needed.

settings.label: Address clients should use (bridge only)
settings.help: For example http://192.168.1.10:32400/. Only used with the bridge network mode; leave empty with host network.

settings.label: Media folder
settings.help: Folder on the data volume that holds your libraries (for example Movies, Series, Music subfolders). It appears as /data inside Plex. It must exist.

settings.label: Media access
settings.help: ro: Plex can only read your media (safe). rw: Plex may also delete files and write sidecar files.

devices.label: Intel Quick Sync (hardware transcoding, needs Plex Pass)

post_install: First start: if you entered a claim token, the server is linked to your Plex account when it first starts. The token is valid for only 4 minutes and the image is downloaded first, so get it (https://www.plex.tv/claim) right before you install, and expect that on a slow connection it may already have expired. The token is optional: without it, open http://<this NAS>:32400/web from a computer in the same network and sign in to claim the server there (with bridge networking or from another subnet, use an SSH tunnel: ssh <user>@<NAS> -L 32400:<NAS address>:32400 -N, then open http://localhost:32400/web). Then add libraries from the media folder (shown as /data). Network: host mode (default) shows Plex on the NAS's own address so LAN discovery (GDM, DLNA) works; it is the less isolated choice. Hardware transcoding needs a Plex Pass and the Intel Quick Sync device switched on here; then enable it in Plex under Settings > Transcoder. Library metadata is kept in /srv/addons/plex/config on the system volume and can grow to tens of GB for large libraries; transcoder files go to /srv/data/addons/plex/transcode.
